title: Scaffold the Cargo package, toolchain pin, lint config, deny.toml and local gate
description:
## Background

The vision bead (omad-vision-8qa, §5.12 and §7 M1 "Project and contract core") fixes the shape of the repository: a single Cargo package with a library and an `omaddons` binary, a pinned stable toolchain, strict lints, `deny.toml`, and one local command that runs the full quality gate (D16: no CI; every commit that changes code runs the gate first). Nothing else in M1 can start until the crate compiles and the gate exists, so this bead lands first and every other M1 bead depends on it.

## Technical Approach

- `Cargo.toml`: package `omaddons`, edition 2024, `publish = false`, `rust-version` equal to the pinned toolchain. `[lib]` plus `[[bin]] name = "omaddons"`.
- Lints in `[lints]`: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`; clippy `unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `dbg_macro`, `print_stdout`, `print_stderr` denied. `clippy.toml` allows unwrap/expect inside `#[test]` code. Integration test crates that need unwrap in helpers add a crate-level `#![allow(...)]`. `print_stdout`/`print_stderr` enforce "commands never print": rendering goes through `src/output/` writing to locked handles via `std::io::Write`.
- Dependencies: every M1 crate from the §5.12 crate table is declared up front with the features the vision names (clap derive/env/wrap_help; serde; serde_json; toml; toml_edit; shell-words; ureq with rustls on the ring provider only; zip with deflate only; sha2; pelite; etcetera; fs4; rustix fs; reflink-copy; tempfile; ulid; jiff; thiserror; schemars). Dev-dependencies: insta, assert_cmd, predicates, proptest. Decided: declaring them once avoids parallel agents fighting over `Cargo.toml` and lets `cargo deny` vet the whole tree in one pass. Crates for later milestones (tar, zstd, sha1, md-5, clap_complete, clap_mangen) are added by the milestone that needs them.
- `rust-toolchain.toml`: pinned to an installed stable release with rustfmt and clippy. Decided: a pinned version instead of the floating `stable` channel so every agent builds with the same compiler.
- `rustfmt.toml` (style edition 2024) and `clippy.toml`.
- `deny.toml`: advisories, a permissive license allowlist (tuned until `cargo deny check` passes), crates.io as the only source, and bans that enforce D9 and the crate table: `openssl-sys`, `native-tls`, `aws-lc-rs`, `aws-lc-sys`, `reqwest`, `tokio`.
- Module skeleton: `src/lib.rs` declares the M1 modules from the §5.12 layout, each file holding only a `//!` doc comment stating its responsibility. Decided: declaring them now keeps parallel beads from colliding on `lib.rs`. `src/net/` is a directory rather than the single `net.rs` the layout shows, because it holds the Http trait, the ureq implementation, the allowlist, net.log, validators, retry and record/replay. Folder classification gets its own `src/inventory.rs`, which the layout does not list.
- The local gate: `Argcfile.sh` recipe `argc gate` calls `scripts/gate.sh`, which runs `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`, `ubs` on changed files (staged, unstaged and untracked relative to HEAD, excluding `.beads/`), and `cargo deny check` only when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed (`--all` forces it).
- `.gitignore` for `target/`, fuzz outputs and coverage files.
- README.md v1 describing exactly what exists: the goal, the pre-alpha status, how to build, the gate, the layout, and where the plan lives.
- A "This Project" section in CLAUDE.md with the gate rule and the crate-level rules (fsx single writer, no printing outside `output`, no unwrap outside tests).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `cargo build` produces `target/debug/omaddons`, and running it exits 0.
- `argc gate --all` passes: fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, tests, ubs and cargo deny.
- `cargo tree -i aws-lc-rs`, `cargo tree -i openssl-sys` and `cargo tree -i tokio` find nothing.
- `rust-toolchain.toml` pins an installed stable toolchain; `cargo --version` inside the repository reports it.
- README.md describes only what exists, and CLAUDE.md has a "This Project" section.
- No `.github/` directory exists (D16).

## Test Plan

- Unit: none (no logic yet).
- E2E: `tests/smoke.rs` runs the built binary with `assert_cmd` and asserts exit 0. The CLI skeleton bead replaces it with the bare-help contract test.
- Gate: run `argc gate --all` and record the output in the close reason.

## Considerations

- ureq's default features may pull in a crypto provider other than ring. Verify with `cargo tree` and disable default features where needed.
- The deny license allowlist must be the minimum the tree actually needs; widen it only in response to a concrete `cargo deny` rejection.
- `cargo deny check` fetches the advisory database over the network; the gate runs it only when dependency files change.

title: omaddons vision, architecture and milestone roadmap (M1–M5)
description:
# omaddons — vision, architecture, milestone roadmap

Living document. Body revision 2, 2026-10-14. This revision incorporates:
- the decisions recorded as comments: D16 (no CI, local gate) and D17–D22 (CLI contract, exit codes, discovery surfaces, doctor, wire-name pinning, politeness constants);
- revision set 2: 28 changes, logged in §11.

Comments added after this revision supersede the body where they conflict. External facts were verified on 2026-10-14 unless marked UNVERIFIED.

## 1. Thesis

`omaddons` is a single Rust binary that is the sole authority over every World of Warcraft client on a Linux machine. That covers:
- Battle.net under Wine/Proton/umu (Omarchy's default);
- Steam, Lutris, Heroic and Bottles prefixes;
- custom private-server clients: 1.12.1, 2.4.3, 3.3.5a (AzerothCore), 4.3.4 and 5.4.8.

It discovers every client and manages addons per client (a "target") through one journaled transaction engine. Everything is exposed through a stable, machine-readable CLI contract. Coding agents drive the CLI directly. Humans use a thin Omarchy bar widget that renders CLI output and holds no logic of its own.

Every mutation is a transaction: install, update, remove, adopt, sync, backup restore and doctor repair. Each one is snapshotted, attributed to an actor, and reversible with `omaddons undo`.

Framing: **the CLI is the product, the widget is a view, the agent skill is the manual.**

## 2. Goals and non-goals

Goals:
- **G1 Multi-target.** All installed flavors are managed simultaneously: retail, progression Classic, Classic Era, Anniversary, Forever, PTR/XPTR/beta. Custom and legacy clients are first-class targets with stable identities.
- **G2 Zero-config, keyless by default.** Discovery needs no setup. The most-used addons install and update without any account. CurseForge and Wago are optional bring-your-own-credential sources; nothing depends on them.
- **G3 Reliability.**
  - No operation can leave an addon half-installed.
  - Crashes recover, and only a process that provably holds the lock repairs anything.
  - Widget, terminal and agent can mutate concurrently, because the lock is held only for milliseconds.
  - Upstream schema drift yields typed errors, never crashes or unparseable output.
- **G4 Agent-first ergonomics.**
  - The first command an agent guesses works.
  - Under `--json`, stdout carries exactly one envelope, success or failure.
  - Every error carries an executable fix (a display string plus `argv`).
  - Plans are stored: a dry run can be applied exactly.
  - Every change is attributed to an actor.
  - Discovery via `capabilities`, `doctor` and `robot-docs`.
  - The skill is installed where agents look. Output is token-frugal.
- **G5 Verifiable privacy.** Hard host allowlist (redirects included), a local request log that also covers git subprocesses, `--offline`, no telemetry, no CurseForge or Wago data persisted.
- **G6 Correct by the game's rules.** Client capabilities (`ClientRules`) are applied to the actual archive contents. Folder identity is case-insensitive, matching Wine.
- **G7 Diagnostics and recovery.**
  - `doctor` follows the world-class doctor contract.
  - Lua errors captured by BugGrabber are attributed to addons.
  - Required dependencies are resolved.
  - `WTF/` can be backed up and restored.
- **G8 Omarchy-native widget** following the house plugin pattern, always version-locked to the binary.

Non-goals:
- No standalone GUI or TUI, no daemon, no MCP server in v1. The command layer returns typed results, so an MCP adapter would be a thin later addition.
- No WeakAuras/Wago string management, no ElvUI profile management, no SavedVariables editing.
  - Whole-`WTF/` backup and restore is in scope; backups never parse or edit contents.
  - `errors` reads BugGrabber's SavedVariables file read-only.
- No Windows or macOS support. Code may stay portable but is untested and unsupported.
- No CurseForge proxy, no bundled API keys.
- No addon authoring or packaging.
- No CI, public distribution or public installer while the repository is private (D16).

## 3. Reference project audit

Reference: https://github.com/BabaStardust/Omarchy-WoW-Addons-Plugin at commit 5c35a8f (v1.1.1, MIT). It is an Omarchy bar widget (`Panel.qml`, ~1000 lines of QML) plus `bin/wowaddons` (750 lines of stdlib Python) calling CurseForge API v1 with a user-supplied key.

The audit found no telemetry or malicious behavior. Network traffic is limited to api.curseforge.com, the CurseForge CDN, and xdg-open of user-clicked links.

Ideas worth keeping:
- argv-only process invocation (no shell);
- the API key passed via stdin and stored mode 0600 with atomic writes;
- zip path-traversal checks and checksum verification;
- honoring `allowModDistribution=false` with a manual-download flow;
- `Text.PlainText` rendering of all API strings in QML.

Defects this design must fix (line references into `bin/wowaddons` / `Panel.qml` at 5c35a8f):

| # | Reference behavior | Consequence | omaddons mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | One AddOns dir resolved by glob plus a folder-name guess; only `*forever*`/`*classic_beta*` folders are auto-picked (`resolve()`, l.132-149). A comment promises a classic fallback that is not implemented | A retail-only install resolves to `no-flavor`. Custom layouts (`drive_c/WoW`) are never detected | Discovery from `product.db`, `.build.info`, `.flavor.info`, drive mappings, launcher configs and PE version; many targets with stable keys (§5.2) |
| R2 | `install_zip` rmtree's previous folders, then per folder rmtree + `os.replace` (l.339-349); state is recorded afterwards | A failure mid-loop leaves an addon partially replaced or deleted, with stale records | `RENAME_EXCHANGE` per-folder swaps, a phased journal, recovery under the lock, snapshot-based undo (§5.5) |
| R3 | `main` catches only `Failure`/`ValueError` (l.741-746) | A KeyError on API drift or an OSError in rmtree prints a traceback and no JSON, so the panel shows "no response". A JSONDecodeError surfaces as "Invalid argument" | Typed error model; one stdout envelope under `--json` even on panic (§5.9) |
| R4 | Read-modify-write of `installed.json` without a lock, using a fixed `.tmp` name (`write_json`, l.99-105) | A concurrent widget and CLI/agent can lose updates or clobber the temp file | The fsx single writer; flock held for the commit window only; per-target generations; unique temp + rename for every write |
| R5 | Zip top-level directories used verbatim (l.331) | `Foo-main/` and `Foo-main/Foo/` layouts install broken | Addon-root detection by TOC; name normalization |
| R6 | File choice = max fileId per gameVersionTypeId; default releaseType 3 = alpha (l.47, l.237-247) | Alpha builds by default; no check that the client will load the file | Pure selection + TOC verification against `ClientRules`; stable channel by default |
| R7 | CurseForge-only with a mandatory key; caches CurseForge search results (l.436-495) | Useless without a CF console key. CF terms forbid caching API data, and say non-developer console accounts may be deleted | Keyless-first; CF opt-in; CF/Wago archives and responses never cached |
| R8 | Each panel open spawns `list` + `config` + `updates` + a featured `search` (two network round trips); ~38 ms Python startup per process (measured with hyperfine) | Latency and network chatter on every open | One local `status --json --cached` read (< 5 ms, no network); background checks; file-change and Hyprland doorbells |
| R9 | Unmanaged addons are only listed. `Blizzard_*` folders in custom clients appear as unmanaged | No adoption; protected folders exposed to mutation | Tiered adoption; `Blizzard_*` protected by a case-insensitive key at the type level |
| R10 | The background update check can `mkdir` the AddOns folder (l.157-160), contradicting the README's "nothing written without a click" | Surprising writes | Read commands never write to game directories; target markers are written only at registration, under the lock |
| R11 | URLs from the API are passed to `xdg-open` unchecked (`Panel.qml` l.109) | Arbitrary scheme handlers are reachable | Widget executes `argv` arrays only; only `https` URLs to allowlisted web hosts are opened |
| R12 | Agent support is an AGENTS.md key-setup walkthrough | No machine contract | Full agent contract (§5.9–5.10) |

Language note: most improvements come from design, not language. Rust is chosen for:
- a self-contained binary with no interpreter dependency;
- ~1–2 ms startup for the high-frequency widget and agent calls;
- type-level enforcement of safety invariants: folder keys that cannot escape AddOns or name protected folders, a closed filesystem `Op` enum, exhaustive error mapping;
- simple bounded concurrency.

## 4. Verified external facts

### 4.1 Battle.net installs

- **Omarchy's install.** Omarchy installs Battle.net via umu-launcher + GE-Proton into `WINEPREFIX=~/Games/battlenet` (`omarchy-install-gaming-battlenet`) and launches it with `omarchy-launch-battlenet`. The WoW root is `~/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft/`.
- **`product.db`.** The Battle.net Agent keeps a protobuf database at `<prefix>/drive_c/ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/product.db`.
  - On the development machine it contains the install path `C:/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft`, the flavor `_retail_` and the version `12.1.0.69933`.
  - The field layout follows WowUp's reader and is UNVERIFIED. A tolerant wire-format reader is sufficient.
- **Drive letters.** `<prefix>/dosdevices/<letter>:` symlinks map Windows drive letters to Linux paths. The development machine has `c: → ../drive_c`, `s: → /home`, `w: → /mnt`, `x: → ~`, `z: → /`. A game installed on another letter lives outside `drive_c`.
- **`<root>/.build.info`** is BPSV: one header row of pipe-separated `Name!TYPE:size` columns, then one row per installed product.
  - Columns have changed over the years (KeyService, KeyRing and Product were added later), so **parse by header name, never by position**.
  - Relevant columns: `Product`, `Version` (e.g. `12.1.5.70391`), `Active` (`1`), `Branch` (`us`/`eu`), `Tags` (contains spaces, `?` and `:`).
  - Example header: `Branch!STRING:0|Active!DEC:1|Build Key!HEX:16|CDN Key!HEX:16|Install Key!HEX:16|IM Size!DEC:4|CDN Path!STRING:0|CDN Hosts!STRING:0|CDN Servers!STRING:0|Tags!STRING:0|Armadillo!STRING:0|Last Activated!STRING:0|Version!STRING:0|KeyRing!HEX:16|Product!STRING:0`.
  - Format reference: https://wowdev.wiki/TACT
- **`.flavor.info`.** Each flavor folder `<root>/_<x>_/` contains `.flavor.info` (BPSV header `Product Flavor!STRING:0`, value = product code). It is the authoritative folder → product mapping.
- **Products.** From Blizzard productconfig `shared_container_default_subfolder`, mirrored at https://github.com/Arctium/bnet-tact-channel-configs. Prior art: instawow `wow_installations.py`, WowUp `warcraft-platform.linux.ts`.

| Product | Folder | Exe | Version (Oct 2026) | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wow | `_retail_` | WoW.exe | 12.1.5.70391 | live |
| wowt | `_ptr_` | WoWT.exe | 12.1.0 | test |
| wowxptr | `_xptr_` | WoWT.exe | 12.1.5 | test |
| wow_beta | `_beta_` | WoWB.exe | 12.0.1 | test |
| wow_classic | `_classic_` | WoWClassic.exe | 5.5.4 (Mists) | live |
| wow_classic_ptr | `_classic_ptr_` | WoWClassicT.exe | 5.5.4 | test |
| wow_classic_beta | `_classic_beta_` | WowB.exe | 1.60.1.70374 (Forever beta) | test |
| wow_classic_era | `_classic_era_` | WoWClassic.exe | 1.15.9 | live |
| wow_classic_era_ptr | `_classic_era_ptr_` | WowClassicT.exe | 2.5.6 (Anniversary PTR) | test |
| wow_anniversary | `_anniversary_` | WoWClassic.exe | 2.5.6 (TBC) | live |
| wow_classic_titan | `_classic_titan_` | WoWClassic.exe | 3.80.2 (China) | live |
| wowf | `_forever_` | Wow.exe | 1.60.1.70245 | live |

- **Product code does not determine game family.** `wow_classic_era_ptr` runs TBC 2.5.x, and `wow_classic_beta` runs Forever 1.60.x. Family is derived from the version; the product is a label and a fallback.
  - Exe names vary in case, so match case-insensitively.
  - Folder names are not derivable by pattern (`wowf` → `_forever_`).
- **Version → family table** (data, overridable in config):
  - Battle.net: major 1 & minor < 50 → `vanilla` (Era); major 1 & minor ≥ 50 → `forever`; 2.5 → `tbc`; 3.4 → `wrath`; 3.80 → `titan`; 4.4 → `cata`; 5.5 → `mists`; major ≥ 6 → `mainline` (retail).
  - Custom (non-Battle.net) clients below the multi-TOC era get `-legacy` families: 1.12.x `vanilla-legacy`, 2.4.x `tbc-legacy`, 3.3.x `wrath-legacy`, 4.3.x `cata-legacy`, 5.4.x `mists-legacy`.
- **Interface number** = major×10000 + minor×100, plus the patch where the client includes it (all current Battle.net clients do):
  - 12.1.5 → 120105; 1.60.1 → 16001; 3.80.2 → 38002.
  - Legacy clients omit the patch: 3.3.5 → 30300, 1.12.1 → 11200, 2.4.3 → 20400, 4.3.4 → 40300, 5.4.8 → 50400.
  - The retail build that started including the patch digit is UNVERIFIED. It doesn't matter for current clients and is encoded per `ClientRules` row (§5.3).
- **Current interfaces** (https://warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/TOC_format): Retail 120105 · Mists Classic 50504 · Classic Era 11509 · Anniversary/TBC 20506 · Titan 38002 · Cata 40402 · Forever 16001 (beta/test).
- **WoW: Forever** ("Classic+", announced at BlizzCon 2026) launches 2026-11-04 with a level cap of 60 and new content.
  - Product `wowf` / folder `_forever_` first appeared in productconfig on 2026-10-13 (uninstall strings "World of Warcraft Forever", "WoW: Forever - Stress Test").
  - The beta currently installs to `_classic_beta_`.
  - The final launch layout is UNVERIFIED, so detection must be data-driven: any new `_x_` folder works without code changes.

### 4.2 Custom and legacy clients

- **Layout:** `<root>/Wow.exe` (any case), `<root>/Interface/AddOns/`, `<root>/WTF/`, and `<root>/Data/<locale>/realmlist.wtf` containing `set realmlist <host>` (location valid 3.0.2–5.0.4, https://warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Realmlist.wtf). There is no `.build.info` and no flavor folder.
- **Versions in use:**
  - 1.12.1, e.g. Turtle WoW — likely the largest private-server population. Its exe version is UNVERIFIED.
  - 2.4.3
  - 3.3.5a (build 12340)
  - 4.3.4
  - 5.4.8
- **Where they live.** A custom client may sit inside a Wine prefix (`drive_c/WoW`) or outside any prefix (`~/Games/<name>/Wow.exe`, run by Lutris, Heroic or Bottles).
- **Version source.** Read the Wow.exe PE `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` numeric fields, not the version string (the string form is UNVERIFIED).
- **`lastAddonVersion`.** `WTF/Config.wtf` `SET lastAddonVersion "<interface>"` is written by the client. On legacy clients it is the most reliable interface source.
- **Protected folders.** Private-server client packs may ship extracted `Blizzard_*` addons inside `Interface/AddOns`. These must never be modified.
- **TOC limits.** Multi-TOC arrived in 9.1.0 / 1.13.7 / 2.5.1 and comma Interface lists in 10.2.7 (the exact matching classic builds are UNVERIFIED). Legacy clients read only `Folder/Folder.toc` with a single Interface value.
  - `Dependencies`, `OptionalDeps` and `LoadOnDemand` predate all of them.
  - `LoadWith` arrived in 1.9 and `LoadManagers` in 2.1.
- **Sources.** No `release.json` flavor and no WoWInterface compatibility tag covers legacy clients. Their sources are GitHub releases and repos, git, URLs and local zips.

### 4.3 TOC format and load rules (https://warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/TOC_format)

- **Basics.** The TOC basename must equal the folder name. The client reads only the first 1024 characters of each line.
- **Game-specific suffixes:** `_Standard` (retail, since 12.1.5), `_Forever` / `_Camelot` (internal game type `camelot`), `_Mists`, `_Cata`, `_Wrath`, `_TBC` (also Anniversary), `_Vanilla`, `_Plunderstorm` / `_WoWLabs`, `_WoWHack`.
- **Family suffixes:** `_Mainline` (standard, forever, plunderstorm, wowhack) and `_Classic` (vanilla…mists).
  - Legacy `_BCC` and `_WOTLKC` are dropped by current clients but appear in the wild.
  - Wago data and managers accept `-` or `_` as the separator.
- **Precedence:** game-specific suffix > family suffix > plain `Name.toc`. Exactly one TOC is loaded.
  - **A Forever client loads a retail-only `_Mainline.toc`** (family Mainline), so verification must also check `## Interface`.
- **Comma lists:** `## Interface: 120105, 50504, 11509` is supported since 10.2.7.
- **Directives:**
  - `Dependencies` (aliases `RequiredDeps` and any directive starting with `Dep`), `OptionalDeps`, `LoadOnDemand`, `LoadWith`, `LoadManagers`, `AllowLoadGameType` / `ExcludeLoadGameType`.
  - Inline file conditionals (`retail.lua [AllowLoadGameType standard]`) and directive conditionals (12.0.7+).
  - Path variables `[Family]`, `[Game]`, `[TextLocale]`.
  - `## Interface-Vanilla:`-style lines are BigWigs-packager build-time only; the client does not read them.
- **Source-identifying fields:** `X-Curse-Project-ID`, `X-WoWI-ID`, `X-Wago-ID`, `X-Tukui-ProjectID`, `X-Tukui-ProjectFolders`, `X-Website`, `X-AddonProvider`, `X-Part-Of`. Also useful: `## Version`, `## Title`, `## Author`, `## Notes`. The packager substitutes `@project-version@` tokens and adds no `X-*` lines.
- **Case-insensitivity under Wine.** Wine resolves file and folder names case-insensitively on case-sensitive Linux filesystems. If two names differ only in case, which one the client loads is undefined. Addon identity is therefore case-insensitive in practice.

### 4.4 WTF, SavedVariables, BugGrabber, running clients

- **SavedVariables paths:**
  - Account: `WTF/Account/<ACCT>/SavedVariables/<Addon>.lua`.
  - Character: `WTF/Account/<ACCT>/<Realm>/<Char>/SavedVariables/<Addon>.lua`.
  - Blizzard's own: `WTF/Account/<ACCT>/SavedVariables.lua`.
  - The client also writes `<Addon>.lua.bak` beside each file.
  - `<ACCT>` is e.g. `123456#1` (Battle.net) or a legacy account name.
  - Account, realm and character names are personal data and never appear in default output.
- **Sizes.** SavedVariables of large addons (WeakAuras, Plater, ElvUI, Details) are commonly 5–50 MB per file. This is typical, not measured, and is multiplied by per-character files.
- **`AddOns.txt`.** Each character folder has `AddOns.txt` (`Name: enabled|disabled`); the modern format is UNVERIFIED.
- **Out-of-date loading.** `WTF/Config.wtf` holds `SET lastAddonVersion "<interface>"`. CVar `checkAddonVersion` (default 1) gates loading out-of-date addons. The "Load out of date AddOns" checkbox resets each patch; where it is stored is UNVERIFIED.
- **When SavedVariables are read and written.** They load just before `ADDON_LOADED` and are written on logout, disconnect, quit and `/reload`. External edits made while the client runs are overwritten.
- **BugGrabber** stores errors in the account SavedVariables file `!BugGrabber.lua`, under the global `BugGrabberDB`.
  - Modern (v12.x): `{session=N, lastSanitation=3, stopnag=?, errors={...}}`, at most 500 errors with the oldest dropped. Each error is `{message=string, stack=string?, locals=string?, session=int, time=unix_epoch_int, counter=int}`. Mirror: https://github.com/hippuli/BugGrabber
  - Legacy r152 (`## Interface: 30300`, common in 3.3.5 packs, e.g. https://github.com/Evolvee/EvolvePWPUI-335a):
    - errors are `{message=string | table of ≤980-char chunks, session, time="%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S", type, counter}`;
    - stack and locals are embedded in `message` after `"\nLocals:|r\n"`;
    - the DB also has `limit=50`, `save` and `throttle`.
  - Stack frames reference `Interface\AddOns\<Folder>\…` (or `/`), which allows attributing errors to folders.
- **Updating while the client runs.**
  - Modern clients pick up new files, new addons and TOC changes on `/reload` (since 9.0.1 retail / 1.14.0 Era). Deleting or renaming a TOC that is already loaded needs a client restart.
  - 3.3.5a, and legacy clients generally, likely need a full restart for new addons or TOC changes (UNVERIFIED).
  - A Linux rename never disturbs files the client already has open.

### 4.5 Addon sources

**GitHub releases + BigWigs packager `release.json`** (https://github.com/BigWigsMods/packager, `upload_github()` in `release.sh`):

### 4.6 Omarchy plugin system

- **Plugins.** A plugin is a folder with `manifest.json` at its root under `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/`. It is loaded into the long-lived `omarchy-shell` (Quickshell/QML), unsandboxed. Saving a file under the plugins directory hot-reloads plugin code.
  - Docs: `~/.local/share/omarchy/shell/README.md`.
  - The schema is enforced by `shell/services/PluginRegistry.qml` and mirrored by `omarchy-plugin-validate`.
- **Validation rules:**
  - `schemaVersion` exactly 1;
  - required `id, name, version, kinds, entryPoints`;
  - id matches `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`, has no `..`, and is not `omarchy.*`;
  - entry points are relative, existing, with no `..`;
  - kinds `bar|bar-widget|menu|overlay|panel|service` each require their entry point (`bar-widget` → `entryPoints.barWidget`);
  - `barWidget.defaultSection` ∈ left|center|right;
  - **no symlinks anywhere in the plugin folder.** This repository contains `AGENTS.md → CLAUDE.md`, so the repository root can never be the plugin.
- **Hidden entries are invisible to the registry.** The third-party scan iterates `"$dir"/*/` (bash globs skip dot-directories), and the hot-reload watcher ignores paths whose first segment starts with `.` (`localPluginIdForPath`). A hidden sibling such as `plugins/.omaddons.stage/` is never treated as a plugin.
- **Non-git install is supported:** write the folder, run `omarchy-shell shell rescanPlugins`, then `omarchy plugin enable <id> [--section …]`. `omarchy plugin update` applies only to git checkouts.
- **House plugin pattern** (a44.herd, a44.beads, a44.docker):
  - Files: `manifest.json` + `Panel.qml` (view) + `Service.qml` (state + `Process` calls) + `Model.js` (pure helpers).
  - The CLI is the authority. An event source is a "doorbell" that triggers a re-fetch of the authority, never a source of state.
  - Settings come from manifest `barWidget.defaults` + `barWidget.schema` (types `string|integer|enum|command|path`).
  - Folders are named for the tool (`plugins/herd`) while ids are namespaced (`a44.herd`).
  - Quickshell `FileView { watchChanges: true }` is available (used in shell `Commons/Style.qml`).
  - Hyprland raw events (`openwindow`, `closewindow`) are consumed through `Quickshell.Hyprland` by the first-party idle service (`plugins/services/idle/Service.qml`).
  - Plugin id for this project: `a44.omaddons`.

### 4.8 Linux and Wine primitives

- **flock.** A lock is tied to an open file description of one inode and is released by the kernel when its holder exits. Renaming or deleting a locked file and then re-creating it yields a different inode, and therefore a second, independent lock.
- **`renameat2(2)`.** `RENAME_EXCHANGE` (atomic swap of two paths) and `RENAME_NOREPLACE` work on btrfs, ext4, xfs and tmpfs. Unsupported filesystems (e.g. NTFS via ntfs-3g, some FUSE) return `EINVAL`. `rustix::fs::renameat_with` exposes them through a safe API.
- **Reflink.** `FICLONE` copies are instant and share space on btrfs and on xfs with `reflink=1`. Elsewhere `reflink-copy` falls back to a byte copy.
- **Process names.** Wine sets the Unix process name (`/proc/<pid>/comm`, 15-character limit) to the Windows exe basename (UNVERIFIED under Proton/umu). `cmdline` and `environ` are the fallback. The `environ` of the user's own processes carries `WINEPREFIX`.

### 5.1 Domain model

- **Install**: a WoW root. Either a Battle.net root (has `.build.info`) or a custom client root (has `Wow*.exe` + `Interface/`, no `.build.info`).
- **Client dir**: the directory that holds `Interface/` and `WTF/`. That is a flavor folder (`<root>/_retail_/`) or a custom root.
- **Target**: one client dir plus its identity `{key, id, install_root, client_dir, flavor_dir?, product?, family, kind: live|test, version, interface, exe_name, label, rules: ClientRules}`.
  - **`key`** is an immutable ULID. It is assigned under the lock at registration: by the first mutating command that touches the target, or by `targets add|rename|default`.
    - It is stored in the registry and mirrored in `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/target.json`. State files are keyed by it.
    - A moved install is re-linked by its marker.
    - A copied install (two live markers with one key) keeps the key at the original path; the copy gets a new key (finding `target-key-duplicate`).
    - Read commands report unregistered targets with `key: null` and a deterministic provisional id, and never write markers.
  - **`id`** is a human alias. Defaults: `retail`, `classic`, `era`, `anniversary`, `forever`, `ptr`, `xptr`, `beta`, `classic-ptr`, `classic-beta`, `era-ptr`, `titan`. Legacy clients take their family name (`vanilla`, `tbc`, `wotlk`, `cata`, `mists`) unless named.
    - The first-discovered target keeps the bare id permanently. Later collisions are qualified (`retail@steam`).
    - `targets rename <id> <new>` exists. `-t` also accepts keys.
  - **`kind`** is `test` for PTR/XPTR/beta products and `live` otherwise.
  - Unknown flavor folders become targets with family `unknown`.
- **Folder**: an `AddOns/<Name>` directory with identity `FolderName::key()`, the ASCII case-folded name. Protection, ownership, collision and duplicate checks all use the key, matching Wine's lookup. Classes:
  - `protected`: key starts with `blizzard_`.
  - `managed`: owned by exactly one managed addon.
  - `linked`: a symlink, e.g. a developer's working copy. Listed, never mutated, never followed outside AddOns.
  - `unmanaged`: everything else.
- **Addon record**: `{ref, name, version, version_confidence: release|toc, release_id, channel, pinned, reason: explicit|dependency, required_by[], folders[], state: ok|degraded, installed_at, tx_id}`. The per-file index lives in `targets/<key>.files.json` (§5.6).
- **Ref**: canonical `source:id`, e.g. `gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2`, `wowi:5108`, `tukui:elvui`, `cf:61284`, `wago:<id>`, `git:<url>[#<rev>]`, `url:<https-zip>`, `file:<path>`.
- **ReleaseSet**: everything one fetch learns about one ref — releases per channel, assets, flavor metadata, hashes, changelog pointers. **Candidate**: one concrete asset selected for one target.
- **Plan**: a resolved, pinned change set `{plan_id, created_at, expires_at, argv, actor, generations{key: n}, ops[], releases[{release_id, url, expected_hash}]}`.
- **Transaction**: one atomic change set on one target.
  - `kind ∈ install|update|remove|undo|adopt|sync|restore|repair`.
  - It is journaled, snapshotted and attributed `{actor, reason?, argv}`.
  - WTF backup creation is recorded in history as `kind: backup` and is not undoable.
- **Finding** (D20): `{id: fm-<subsystem>-<slug>, severity: P0–P3, confidence, target?, addon?, folder?, title, evidence, remediation{command, argv, explain_command, auto_fixable, estimated_actions}}`. P0–P3 is used everywhere, including the `status` severity buckets.
- **ClientRules**: §5.3.

### 5.2 Discovery

1. **Hints, in order:**
   - (a) Battle.net `product.db` per prefix (`drive_c/ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/product.db`). It is parsed by a hand-written tolerant protobuf wire reader (~100 lines). Install paths are mapped through `<prefix>/dosdevices/<letter>:` symlinks. A parse failure falls through to scanning.
   - (b) Launcher configs:
     - Lutris game configs `~/.config/lutris/games/*.yml` (`exe`, `prefix`; newer releases may use `~/.local/share/lutris/games/`, UNVERIFIED);
     - Heroic `GamesConfig/*.json` (`winePrefix`), native and Flatpak;
     - Steam `libraryfolders.vdf`, native and Flatpak (`~/.var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam`);
     - Bottles, native and Flatpak.

     Each format gets a small tolerant reader that extracts keys; there is no general YAML or VDF dependency.
   - (c) Running processes: `WINEPREFIX` and the exe path of matching processes (step 8).
   - (d) `extra_roots` from config.
2. **Bounded scan.** Candidate prefixes are `~/Games/*`, `~/.wine`, Steam compatdata `*/pfx` in every library, and the prefixes from (b). The scan goes `DISCOVERY_MAX_DEPTH` deep and skips `DISCOVERY_SKIP_DIRS`. It runs under each prefix's `drive_c` and under `~/Games` itself (for custom clients outside prefixes), looking for `World of Warcraft/` or any directory containing a `Wow*.exe` (case-insensitive).
3. **Battle.net roots.** Parse `.build.info` by header name and enumerate the `_*_` folders. For each one:
   - product from `.flavor.info` (fallback: `product.db`, then the `.build.info` product table);
   - version, family, interface and `kind`;
   - the exe name from the folder listing;
   - the `ClientRules` row.
4. **Custom roots.** Read the version from PE `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` (`pelite`) and pick the `ClientRules` row. AddOns live at `<root>/Interface/AddOns`. The label comes from the `Data/*/realmlist.wtf` host (`127.0.0.1` → "localhost").
   - On legacy targets, `WTF/Config.wtf lastAddonVersion` overrides the computed interface when present.
   - On Battle.net targets, the `.build.info` interface wins, and a differing `lastAddonVersion` yields the warning `client_not_launched_since_patch`.
5. **Manual targets:** `omaddons targets add <path> [--name N]` (a root, a flavor folder or an AddOns path is accepted and normalized), `targets rm`, `targets rename`, `targets default`.
6. **Discovery cache.** The cache key per root is the (path, size, mtime) of `.build.info`, each `.flavor.info`, `Wow*.exe` and `product.db`, plus the root directory listing. A directory mtime does not change when `.build.info` is rewritten in place, which is why the files are keyed individually. `targets --rescan` forces a full rescan. Unknown flavors and version/interface disagreements produce warnings, not failures.
7. **Registration.** Keys, ids and markers are written only under the lock (§5.1). Discovery itself never writes to game directories.
8. **Running detection** is computed live on every call, including `status --cached`.
   - Read `/proc/<pid>/comm` of the user's own processes.
   - Only for names matching a known exe basename (case-insensitive, aware of 15-character truncation) read `cmdline` and `environ`, and map `WINEPREFIX` / the exe path to a target.
   - Cost is about 1–2 ms.

### 5.3 TOC engine and ClientRules

- **`ClientRules`** is a data table keyed by version range and install kind (`battlenet|custom`).
  - Fields: `multi_toc`, `comma_interface`, `game_suffixes[]`, `family_suffixes[]`, `legacy_suffixes[]`, `directive_conditionals`, `path_variables`, `interface_includes_patch`, `legacy`.
  - Rows:
    - modern Battle.net retail, every Classic family, Forever;
    - legacy 1.12.x, 2.4.x, 3.3.x, 4.3.x, 5.4.x.
  - Rows are overridable in config. **No client version is special-cased in code.**
- **`loaded_toc(folder, &ClientRules, game) -> Option<Toc>`** implements the §4.3 precedence (game-specific > family > plain) for multi-TOC rows, and plain-only for legacy rows.
  - It accepts `-` or `_` separators and the legacy `_BCC`/`_WOTLKC` suffixes where the row lists them.
  - TOC filenames and every file reference resolve case-insensitively.
- **Parser rules:**
  - 1024-character line limit, directives, X- fields; conditionals are recognized.
  - Comma Interface lists apply only where `comma_interface`. Legacy rows parse the leading integer (UNVERIFIED client behavior) and warn `toc_comma_on_legacy`.
- **Compatibility verdict:**
  - a loaded TOC exists;
  - its Interface belongs to the target's family;
  - the interface is not below the family floor (out-of-date loads are allowed, with a warning);
  - `## Interface` decides, not just the suffix (the Forever-loads-`_Mainline` guard).
- **Tests.** Every `ClientRules` row has fixtures. A modern `classic`-flavor build never verifies against a 1.12.1 client.

### 5.4 Sources, selection and dependencies

```rust
trait Source {
    fn id(&self) -> SourceId;
    fn fetch(&self, refs: &[Ref], http: &dyn Http) -> Vec<Result<ReleaseSet>>;  // network; batched; once per distinct ref per run
    fn search(&self, q: &str, http: &dyn Http) -> Result<Vec<Hit>>;             // optional
}
fn select(set: &ReleaseSet, t: &Target, ch: Channel) -> Vec<Candidate>;        // pure, per target
fn verify(archive: &Inspected, t: &Target) -> Verdict;                         // pure TOC load-rule check
```

- **Fetch once.** `install`, `outdated`, `update` and `sync` de-duplicate refs across all targets, fetch each ref once, then select per target. `select` and `verify` are table-tested with no I/O.
- **Ref parsing** accepts:
  - canonical refs;
  - pasted URLs (GitHub repo/release, WoWInterface `info<id>-…`, CurseForge project, Tukui);
  - `git:` URLs with an optional `#tag|branch|sha`;
  - https zip URLs and local paths;
  - installed addon names, and catalog names and aliases.

  Ambiguity returns `ref_ambiguous` with candidates.
- **Built-in catalog.**
  - Sources: `catalog/catalog.toml`, embedded with `include_str!`; user overrides in `~/.config/omaddons/catalog.d/*.toml`.
  - Entry shape: `{name, aliases[], ref, families[], folders[], notes}`.
  - Coverage: popular keyless addons (so `omaddons install weakauras` works without accounts) and verified repos for each legacy family.
  - Its `folders[]` give the folder index used by dependency resolution and adoption.
- **Selection.**
  1. Source metadata yields candidates: `release.json` flavors/interfaces, Tukui `patch[]`, WoWI `UICompatibility`, CF `latestFilesIndexes`.
  2. Each candidate archive is downloaded (blob cache; CurseForge/Wago archives go to the stage directory only), inspected and verified (§5.3).
  3. A failing candidate falls back to the next one.
  - No compatible candidate ⇒ `no_compatible_release`.
  - A user-specified file, URL or zip that does not verify ⇒ `wrong_flavor`.
- **Channels:** `stable` (default) | `beta` | `alpha`, settable per addon. A GitHub prerelease is beta; CF releaseType maps 1/2/3.
- **GitHub main path, with no REST:**
  - the stable tag comes from `releases/latest` (302, not followed) or `releases.atom` (conditional GET with ETag);
  - `release.json` and the asset come from `releases/download/<tag>/<file>`.
  - REST is used only for beta/alpha channels (the prerelease flag), repos without `release.json` (asset listing), and search.
  - With the opt-in token (`omaddons auth github --from-gh` or `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN`), one GraphQL query fetches the latest releases for all tracked repos.
- **Git refs.**
  - GitHub-hosted branch heads come from `https://github.com/<o>/<r>/commits/<branch>.atom` (in-process, so allowlisted and logged).
  - Other hosts use `git ls-remote` with https only, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `-c http.followRedirects=false`, logged as a `via: git` entry in `net.log`.
  - Archives come from `codeload.github.com` for GitHub, and from `git clone --depth 1 --branch` of the working tree for other hosts.
- **Dependencies.** For the TOC the target will load, each absent `Dependencies`/`RequiredDeps`/`Dep*` folder resolves through this chain:
  1. the managed set;
  2. the catalog folder index;
  3. Tukui `directories`;
  4. WoWI `UIDir`, ranked by single-folder project, target compatibility, downloads, then recency;
  5. otherwise a `missing_dependency` warning with candidates.

  Rules:
  - Dependencies on `Blizzard_*` folders are satisfied by the client.
  - Folders shipped in the same archive satisfy each other.
  - Resolved dependencies install in the same transaction with `reason: dependency, required_by: [...]`.
  - `OptionalDeps` never auto-install. `--no-deps` opts out.
  - `remove` of a required addon succeeds with a warning listing its dependents. Dependencies no longer required surface as `orphan`.
- **Search** (M2) covers the catalog, the WoWI index, Tukui and GitHub repo lookups. Ranking: exact/alias match first, then downloads and recency, with per-target compatibility flags and source attribution.

### 5.5 Transaction engine and fsx

**fsx, the single writer.** Every filesystem mutation in the program lives in `src/fsx/`; a test fails if `std::fs` write/rename/remove/create calls appear anywhere else.
- **Closed `Op` enum:** `WriteFile{content, mode}` · `AppendFile{content}` · `CreateDir` · `Rename{to, mode: Replace|NoReplace|Exchange}` · `CloneFile{from}` (reflink with byte-copy fallback) · `Chmod{mode}` · `SymlinkAtomic{target}`.
- **`mutate(path, op)`** follows the doctor contract's order:
  1. scope, op and precondition check;
  2. before-hash;
  3. verbatim backup for file ops, verified byte-identical, into the transaction's snapshot;
  4. in-memory plan;
  5. atomic execution (temp + fsync + rename, or a flagged rename);
  6. after-hash;
  7. an fsync'd `actions.jsonl` line `{path, op, before_hash, after_hash, started_at_ns, finished_at_ns, tx, ok}`.

  Directory ops record tree hashes derived from the per-file index: computed during extraction for new folders, taken from the existing index for managed folders, computed on demand otherwise.
- **Deletion is not an op.** `fsx::prune()` is the only deletion path. It may be called only by:
  - retention pruning;
  - post-commit cleanup of stage dirs and CurseForge/Wago archives;
  - plan expiry;
  - `backup prune`;
  - `doctor gc`.

  Doctor fixers never call it (enforced by test; doctor `allowed_ops` excludes it). Pruning first renames its victim into `<…>/.omaddons/trash/` under the lock, then deletes outside the lock.

**Write-scope table** (enforced by fsx; anything else is refused with exit 4):

| Scope | Writers |
|---|---|
| `~/.config/omaddons/` | `config set`, `auth`, doctor |
| `~/.local/state/omaddons/` | every mutating command, doctor |
| `~/.cache/omaddons/` | every command (derived data) |
| `<client dir>/Interface/AddOns/<folder>` for non-protected keys | install engine, doctor |
| `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/` (stage, snapshots, trash, backups, `target.json`) | install engine, `backup`, doctor |
| `<client dir>/WTF/Account/**/SavedVariables/<owned folder>.lua[.bak]` (account and per-character) | install-engine undo only |
| `<client dir>/WTF/` (whole tree) | `backup restore` only |
| `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/omaddons/` and `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/.omaddons.stage/` | `omarchy install`, `omarchy remove`, doctor |
| `~/.claude/skills/omaddons/` (or the `--dir` given at install) | `robot-docs install-skill`, doctor |

Never writable: any folder whose key starts with `blizzard_`, game executables and data, anything else inside a Wine prefix, and the global lock file (deny-list).

**Locks.**
- **Global lock: `~/.local/state/omaddons/lock`.**
  - Created once; never renamed, truncated away, quarantined or deleted by anything, including `gc`.
  - The holder overwrites its contents in place (same inode) with `{pid, command, started_at}`, for diagnosis only.
  - Held only for revalidate → journal → swap → commit (milliseconds), never across network I/O.
  - The acquire timeout is `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT`.
- **In-flight locks.** Each transaction holds a flock on `~/.local/state/omaddons/inflight/<tx>.lock` from planning until cleanup. Stage dirs, temporary blobs and stored plans carry the tx or plan id. An artifact is orphaned only if its in-flight lock is free or missing. A held flock is the only proof of liveness anywhere in the program.
- **Generations.** Each target record carries `generation`, incremented by every commit.

**Steps:**
1. **Plan** (no lock). Resolve every requested change against a state snapshot that records each target's `generation`, and compute folder adds/replaces/removes and dependency installs. The output is the plan, which is what `--dry-run` returns (stored per §5.9).
2. **Download** (no lock) to `~/.cache/omaddons/blobs/<sha256>`. The cache is content-addressed, so reinstall, undo and cross-target copies work offline; CurseForge/Wago archives go to the stage dir only. Verify source hashes where provided (CF sha1, WoWI md5).
3. **Inspect archive** (no lock).
   - Addon roots are directories containing a TOC that matches their own name (any recognized suffix, case-insensitive).
   - Normalize `Foo-main/` / `Foo-master/` and version-suffixed roots by TOC name; descend through single wrapper directories; ignore loose root files.
   - Reject: absolute paths, drive letters, `..`, symlink entries, device entries, entries whose case-folded paths collide, more than `ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES` entries, more than `ARCHIVE_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED`, and a compression ratio above `ARCHIVE_MAX_RATIO`.
4. **Ownership check** (no lock; repeated in step 6). Enforced by `FolderName`, which cannot represent `/`, `..`, a leading `.`, or a key starting with `blizzard_` in the mutable namespace.
   - A folder owned by another managed addon ⇒ `ownership_conflict`.
   - Any protected key ⇒ `protected_folder`; there is no override.
   - An unmanaged folder ⇒ `unmanaged_folder` (fix: `adopt`).
   - A new folder whose key matches an existing folder with a different spelling ⇒ `case_collision` (exit 4; `fix` names the existing folder plus `adopt`/`remove`).
   - `--force` on `ownership_conflict` moves the folder to the new addon and marks the previous owner `degraded` (finding `ownership-transferred`). Both records are part of the transaction, so undo restores both. `--force` on `unmanaged_folder` snapshots the unmanaged folder and replaces it.
5. **Stage** (no lock). Extract under `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/stage/<tx>/`. This is on the same filesystem as AddOns, outside the directory the client scans, and unique per transaction.
6. **Lock and revalidate.** Acquire the global lock and run recovery (below). If any affected target's `generation` changed since step 1, re-check ownership and folder state without network (archives are already staged) and re-plan once. If it still conflicts, fail with `plan_stale` (exit 1, retryable).
7. **Journal and SavedVariables snapshot.**
   - Write the journal `prepared` (fsync).
   - `CloneFile` the touched folders' SavedVariables into `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/WTF/…`: account and per-character `SavedVariables/<Folder>.lua` and `.lua.bak`. On btrfs and xfs this is instant and uses no extra space.
   - Snapshot the target's state files into `~/.local/state/omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/`.
8. **Swap.** Before each rename, append and fsync a step record to the journal.
   - **Replacement:** `RENAME_EXCHANGE` staged ⇄ live, then rename the now-staged old version into `snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/`.
   - **New folder:** `RENAME_NOREPLACE` staged → live, so a folder created after planning is never overwritten.
   - **Removal:** rename live → `snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/`.
   - Parent directories are fsync'd after each phase.
   - On `EINVAL`/`ENOSYS`, fall back to two renames under the journal and report `atomic_swap: false` for that target.
   - The journal then becomes `swapped`.
9. **Commit.**
   - Write the target record with `generation + 1` and the per-file index.
   - Append `history.jsonl` and mark the journal `committed`.
   - Release the lock.
   - Afterwards: rewrite `status.json` (monotonic, §5.6), delete the journal, prune the stage dir, and run retention.

**Journal phases and recovery.**
- Phases run `prepared` → one step record per rename → `swapped` → `committed`. Recovery rolls forward from `swapped`, rolls back from anything earlier, and reads the step records instead of inferring progress from which directories exist.
- A journal counts as left over only when the process examining it holds the global lock: a held flock proves the writer is alive, a free one proves it is gone. Mutating commands recover right after acquiring the lock and report `journal_recovered`.
- Read commands never recover. They list `journal/`, probe the lock with a non-blocking `try_lock`, and add the warning `journal_pending` (lock free) or `tx_in_progress` (lock held), each with a `fix`.
- Journals in phase `committed` are complete. Their writer or the next lock holder deletes them, and they are never reported.

**Undo.**
- `omaddons undo` reverts the most recent transaction; `undo <tx>` reverts an older one only if no later transaction of any kind (including `repair` and `adopt`) touched the same folders, otherwise `undo_conflict`. `undo --last-by <actor>` reverts that actor's most recent transaction.
- The output always names the transaction being reverted.
- Undo is itself a transaction, snapshotted, so it can be undone.
- Folders and state records are restored. SavedVariables follow `--saved-variables auto|restore|keep`:
  - `auto` (the default), per file:
    - unchanged since the tx ⇒ nothing to do (the new code never ran);
    - changed ⇒ the current file is cloned into the undo transaction, then restored, so nothing is lost;
    - client running ⇒ the SavedVariables part is skipped and reported as `saved_variables_deferred`, with `fix: omaddons undo <tx> --saved-variables restore` once the client exits. Folders follow the running policy.
  - `restore`: like `auto`, but refused with `game_running` instead of deferred while the client runs.
  - `keep`: SavedVariables are never touched.
- SavedVariables are never written while the target's client runs, under any policy or flag.

**Running policy** (`running_policy = "safe" | "refuse" | "allow"`, default `safe`).
- While a target's client runs, `safe` allows replacing folders whose TOC basenames are unchanged, and adding folders.
- It refuses with `game_running` (exit 4):
  - removing or renaming folders with a loaded TOC;
  - SavedVariables restores;
  - any mutation on a `legacy` client.
- `--while-running` overrides the folder rules but never the SavedVariables rule.
- Every mutation outcome carries `reload_required: none|reload|restart` per target.

**Retention.**
- Snapshots younger than 24 h are never pruned.
- Beyond that, keep the last 10 per target within 7 days, capped at `SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES` per target, oldest first, and never the most recent transaction.
- Age protection wins over the size cap. If young snapshots alone exceed the cap, the warning `snapshot_cap_exceeded` is raised.
- The blob cache is LRU-capped at `BLOB_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`. Blobs referenced by retained transactions, installed records or unexpired plans are pinned.
- CurseForge/Wago undo uses snapshots, never blobs.

**Invariant.** At every instant, each AddOns folder is either the complete old version or the complete new version.
- This holds exactly where `atomic_swap: true`, and across crashes via the journal otherwise.
- Multi-folder addons are consistent across crashes via the journal. A `/reload` during a running-client transaction may briefly see mixed folders, so the final outcome reports `reload_required`.

### 5.7 Network and privacy

- **One HTTP client:** `ureq` with rustls and the `ring` provider, behind an `Http` trait with real, fixture-replay and record implementations.
- **Host allowlist.** Enforced on every request and every redirect hop:
  - always: `api.github.com`, `github.com`, `codeload.github.com`, `objects.githubusercontent.com`, `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`, `api.mmoui.com`, `cdn.wowinterface.com`, `api.tukui.org`;
  - when enabled: `api.curseforge.com`, `edge.forgecdn.net`, `mediafilez.forgecdn.net`, `addons.wago.io`;
  - plus git hosts the user configures.

  Violations ⇒ `host_blocked`. Git subprocesses are restricted to allowlisted https hosts with redirects disabled.
- **Logging and offline mode.** Every HTTP request and git subprocess is logged to `net.log`, and `omaddons net-log [--since]` renders it. `--offline` (or `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`) makes any network attempt fail fast with `offline`.
- **Hygiene.** No telemetry. User-Agent `omaddons/<version>`. Credentials are never logged, never placed in the argv of child processes, and never printed.
- **What privacy can't cover.** An update check reveals the checked addons to the queried source; with a GitHub token or CF key it is attributable to that account.
- **GitHub without REST** is the main path (§5.4). REST and GraphQL are used only as described there.
- **The GitHub token is opt-in:** `omaddons auth github --from-gh` reads `gh auth token` once, on explicit request; otherwise `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN`. `GITHUB_TOKEN` is never read implicitly.
- **Efficiency:**
  - CF: one `POST /v1/mods` batch.
  - WoWI: comma-batched `filedetails`.
  - Tukui: one list call.
  - GitHub: tags from atom/redirects with validators, assets from release URLs.
  - Every ref is fetched once per run, with bounded parallelism.
  - Every limit comes from §5.13.
- **CurseForge/Wago compliance.** Neither archives nor response bodies are cached or persisted. Archives live only in stage dirs and are deleted at commit. The only data at rest is the mod id, file id and version string inside install records.

### 5.8 Status, doctor, errors and backup

**`status` (triage).** One call returns:
- every target: family, version, interface, kind, key/id;
- pending update counts;
- doctor findings summarized by severity (P0–P3);
- recent Lua error counts;
- live running state, journal warnings;
- a `commands` list of recommended next actions.

`status --cached` reads local state only, in under 5 ms with no network: records, last `outdated` results, last drift result, and live running state. It never runs drift or network checks. `status --check` exits 6 when any target needs attention.

**`omaddons doctor`** diagnoses broken on-disk state that omaddons owns or manages, and repairs it only with consent and reversibly. The contract follows `~/skills/global/skills/world-class-doctor-mode-for-cli-tools/references/{DOCTOR-CONTRACT,SAFETY-CONTRACT,KERNEL}.md`; this section pins the omaddons-specific choices.
- **Surface.**
  - Verbs: `doctor [diagnose]` (default, read-only), `fix` (and `--fix`), `undo <run|latest>`, `explain <finding-id>`, `capabilities`, `health`, `robot-docs`, `ls`, `diff [<run>]`, `gc --before <date> --yes`.
  - Flags: `--json`, `--robot`, `--quiet`, `-v`, `--no-color`, `--no-progress`, `--dry-run`, `--only`, `--skip`, `--since`, `--online`, `--severity`, `--budget`, `--quick`, `--include-deep`, `--robot-triage`, `--force` (requires `--yes` at the parser level), `--yes`.
  - Bare `doctor` never mutates.
- **Findings.**
  - Each id has the form `fm-<subsystem>-<symptom-slug>`; severity is P0–P3.
  - Each finding carries a `confidence`, concrete `evidence` (path, hash, observed vs expected) and a `remediation` (`command`, `argv`, `explain_command`, `auto_fixable`, `estimated_actions`).
  - Reports carry a terminal `state`: `DONE_OK | DONE_FINDINGS | DONE_PARTIAL | DONE_FAILED | REFUSING | LOCK_LOST | ABORTED`.
  - `health` prints one line whose first token is `ok | findings | unsafe | concurrency`.
- **JSON shape.** Doctor JSON uses the doctor-contract report shapes at the top level. They also include the general envelope keys (`ok`, `schema_version`, `tool_version`, `command`, `exit_code`, `warnings`, `commands`), so generic envelope consumers still work.
- **Three hard rules.**
  1. **One writer.** Every write under `--fix` goes through `fsx::mutate()` (§5.5).
  2. **Never delete.** Removal means renaming into the run's `quarantine/`. `doctor gc --before <date> --yes` is the only doctor surface that deletes, and it deletes only old run directories.
  3. **Never fix without consent.** `--fix`/`fix` are explicit; `--only <fm-id>` scopes a fix.
- **One transaction engine, two views.**
  - A doctor fix run is one `repair` transaction in the shared journal and `history.jsonl`, so there is one recovery path and one crash-injection matrix.
  - `omaddons doctor undo <run>` resolves to `omaddons undo <tx>`. Undo-conflict detection spans install and repair transactions.
  - The run folder holds `report.json`, `actions.jsonl` (written by fsx), `backups/` and `quarantine/` (the repair transaction's snapshot for paths under omaddons' own directories), and an idempotent `undo.sh` that calls `omaddons doctor undo <run>`.
  - Paths inside a client dir are snapshotted same-filesystem under `snapshots/<tx>/` and referenced from `actions.jsonl`.
  - A `latest` symlink is updated with `SymlinkAtomic`.
- **Safety envelope.**
  - Doctor write scopes are the §5.5 table minus every `WTF/` row: the doctor never touches `WTF/`.
  - It uses the global lock (`LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT`, then exit 5).
  - Network only with `--online`; without it, online checks are skipped or return exit 6.
  - No destructive shell commands. No prompts and no ANSI under `--robot`.
- **Subsystems and the initial failure-mode catalog** (auto-fixable ones marked *):

| Subsystem | Failure modes |
|---|---|
| `concurrency_primitives` | `lock-held-long` (manual: reports holder pid/command/age from the lock file's contents; fix = wait or end that process; the file is never touched) · `journal-pending`* (unrecovered journal → roll forward/back, P0) · `orphan-inflight`* (stage dirs, temp blobs or plans whose in-flight lock is free → quarantine) |
| `schemas` | `state-version-older`* (migrate) · `state-version-newer` (P0; refuse writes; manual: upgrade binary) |
| `state_files` | `status-stale`* (regenerate) · `history-torn-line`* (rewrite without the partial tail, backed up) · `record-folder-missing` (manual: reinstall or forget) · `record-target-missing` |

| `external_artifacts` | `nested-addon-folder`* (flatten via Rename) · `orphan-snapshot-dir`* · `managed-files-modified` (manual: reinstall; lists files) · `ownership-conflict` · `ownership-transferred` · `case-collision` · `duplicate-addon` · `wrong-flavor` · `out-of-date-toc` · `missing-dependency` (manual, command given) |

- **What doctor does not report.** "Update available" and "Lua errors" are status, not broken state; they belong to `outdated`, `errors` and `status`. Before the doctor surface lands (M4), `journal-pending` and `state-version-*` are detected by the engine and reported as plain warnings.
- **Safety harness** (part of the local gate from M4):
  - reversibility: fix → undo → byte-identical;
  - idempotence: a second `--fix` takes 0 actions;
  - crash recovery: kill at every `mutate()` step;
  - concurrency: two fixers, one lock;
  - detector repeatability: the same state gives the same findings.

  Every auto-fixer ships a fixture under `tests/doctor_fixtures/<fm-id>/` that round-trips: corrupt → fix → assert → undo → compare against the corrupted snapshot.

**`errors`** (`omaddons errors [-t T] [--since 1d] [--addon A]`).
- Parses both BugGrabber schemas (§4.4) with a SavedVariables literal-table parser. It handles a subset of Lua: `Name = <table>` assignments, tables with `[key] = value` and positional entries, strings with Lua escapes and long brackets, numbers, booleans and nil. Input is capped at `SAVEDVARIABLES_MAX_BYTES`.
- Groups errors by attributed folder, then by managed addon.
- Reports count, first/last seen, the latest message with a trimmed stack, the installed version and any available update.
- Raw `locals` are omitted unless `--verbose`, since they may contain personal data.

**`backup`** (`omaddons backup [create | list | restore <id> | export <id> <file.tar.zst> | prune] [-t T]`).
- `create` reflink-snapshots `WTF/` into `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/backups/<ts>/`.
- `export` writes a tar.zst, because same-disk copies do not survive a disk failure.
- `restore` is an undoable `restore` transaction that snapshots the current `WTF/` first, and is refused while the client runs.
- `auto_backup = "daily"` (default `off`) takes a backup before the day's first mutation of a target.
- Output shows counts and sizes only; account, realm and character names never appear.

### 5.9 CLI contract (frozen at first ship)

The contract is completed in M4 and frozen at the first tagged release. After that, changes follow §5.12's wire-name rules.

- **The first command an agent guesses should work.** Bare `omaddons` prints concise help to stdout and exits 0. The help lists the most common verbs, the discovery trio (§5.10) and the exit-code table. It never runs an action, never opens a pager or TUI, and never prompts. Bare `omaddons --json` prints the same information as JSON.
- **stdout is data and stderr is diagnostics.**
  - **stdout:** under `--json` / `--format json` / `--robot` / `OMADDONS_FORMAT=json`, exactly one envelope, success or failure. Otherwise human-formatted data, and empty on error. Help and `robot-docs` output are data.
  - **stderr:** NDJSON when stderr is not a TTY, or `CI` is set, or `TERM=dumb`; every line is then an object with `event` ∈ `progress|log|warning|error`. On an interactive TTY, stderr carries human lines (`warning: …`, `error[<code>]: <message> / fix: <fix>`, progress bars).
  - Every error is mirrored to stderr as one line: `{"event":"error",…}` or the human form.
  - Progress events appear only with `--progress json` (or as human progress on a TTY). `--progress json|human|none` is the explicit control.
- **Envelope.** One shape for success and failure:
  ```json

  ```
  - **Fixes.** `fix` is required and never empty; internal errors use `omaddons doctor`. Display strings are shell-quoted (`shell-words`). Every `fix`, `alternatives[]` entry, `commands[]` entry and finding `remediation` carries `argv`.
  - **Executing.** Programs execute `argv` only. The widget executes only entries whose `argv[0]` is `omaddons`, substituting its configured binary path. Non-CLI fixes such as `/reload in game` carry `argv: null`.
  - **Assertion failures** (`--check`, `--strict`, exit 6) return `ok:false` with `data` still populated and `error.code = "check_failed"`.
  - **Panics.** A panic hook still emits a well-formed envelope (`code: internal`, exit 1) on stdout under `--json`, mirrored on stderr.
  - **Doctor** uses its contract shapes at the top level, including these envelope keys (§5.8).
- **Every command offers `--json`.** This includes `help`, `completions` (`{"shell","script"}`), `robot-docs` (`{"format":"markdown","content"}`) and every doctor verb. `--json` implies `--no-color` and `--no-progress`.
- **Terminal handling.** Honor `NO_COLOR`, `CI` (which also forces non-interactive mode and disables progress), `TERM=dumb`, `--no-color`, `--no-progress` and non-TTY detection.
- **Determinism.** Under `--json`, output is deterministic: struct keys in declaration order, map keys sorted, stable list order. Volatile fields live only in `meta`.
- **Token-frugal by default.** JSON contains ids, names, versions and counts; `--verbose` adds evidence, changelogs and paths.

**Behavior:**
- **Stored plans.** Every mutating command supports `--dry-run`. It returns the plan in the same `data` schema the real run returns, plus a `plan_id` (stored under `plans/`, `PLAN_TTL` 24 h; pinned release ids, URLs, expected hashes, target generations) and `commands: [apply]`. `apply <plan_id>` executes exactly that plan, or fails with `plan_stale` if any generation or pinned release no longer matches. The widget applies the plan it displayed.
- **Desired state.** `addons.toml` has per-family sections, which apply to every `live` target of that family, and optional per-target sections (`[target.<id>]`), which are the only way to address `test` targets. Entries are refs with optional pins/versions.
  - `sync` reconciles desired vs installed in one transaction per target and is idempotent.
  - `--prune` removes unlisted managed addons; `--locked` installs exact versions.
  - `export` writes the file. `copy --from --to` installs the same refs where compatible and reports skips.
- **Target defaults.**
  - Read commands, `outdated`, `update`, `errors` and `doctor` default to all targets.
  - `install` defaults to the configured default target, else the single compatible target, else `target_ambiguous` with candidates and exact commands.
  - `-t` accepts a target id, key, family name, product code (`wow_classic_era`), flavor folder name (`_retail_`), install root, or AddOns path.
- **Idempotent.** Installing an already-current addon, or updating with nothing to update, is `ok` with an empty change list. Installing an installed addon whose release is newer updates it (`kind: update`).
- **CurseForge manual downloads.** `install <ref> --file <zip>` installs a manually downloaded archive as that ref's release after verifying it against the source's expected hash. When omitted after `distribution_disabled`, the expected file name is looked up in `~/Downloads`.
- **No prompts.** Nothing prompts without a TTY, and nearly nothing prompts at all, because mutations are undoable. `--force` only overrides the protections listed in §5.5 step 4; it never applies to protected folders.
- **Attribution.** Every mutating command records `actor`, `reason` and `argv` in history (§5.6).

- **Discovery trio:** `omaddons capabilities --json`, `omaddons doctor --json`, `omaddons robot-docs guide`.

- **`robot-docs`.**
  - `guide`: the Markdown handbook. Contents: CLI surface, exit-code tables, error codes with fixes, the safety model (dry-run/apply, undo, running policy, protected folders, actor attribution) with a "will never do" list, and recipes for the canonical intents.

- **Intent inference.**

- **Canonical intents**, each ≤ 2 commands with JSON output:
  - update everything;
  - what is broken (`status`, then `doctor` or `errors`);
  - install X for target Y;
  - add a legacy addon from a git repo;
  - preview, then apply exactly (`--dry-run`, `apply`);
  - undo what the agent did today (`history --actor agent --since 1d`, `undo --last-by agent`);
  - explain pending updates with changelogs;
  - restore a fresh machine (`sync`).

- Changing them:

## 6. Decisions and rationale

| ID | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Rust single binary | No interpreter dependency; ms startup for frequent widget/agent calls; type-level safety invariants; easy bounded concurrency |
| D2 | The CLI is the product; the widget is a view | Agents and humans share one contract and one implementation; the widget cannot drift into holding logic |
| D3 | No daemon, no MCP in v1 | Nothing needs to run continuously; agents drive CLIs natively; MCP would duplicate schemas; the typed command layer keeps a later adapter thin |
| D4 | Keyless-first; CurseForge/Wago opt-in | CF terms make user keys fragile (non-transferable, no caching, non-developer accounts deletable); Wago needs a paid token; the most-used addons ship on GitHub, WoWI and Tukui |
| D5 | Verify TOCs inside the archive | Upstream metadata is wrong in practice (WeakAuras has no mainline entry); the client's own load rules are ground truth; required for legacy clients, which have no metadata |
| D6 | Journaled transactions with snapshots | Crash-recoverable, and enables cheap undo, which is what makes agent autonomy safe |
| D7 | Stage, snapshots and backups under `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/` | The same filesystem as AddOns and WTF guarantees atomic renames and reflinks; it is outside the client's scan path |
| D8 | JSON state + flock, not SQLite | Small data, inspectable, no C dependency; atomic replace is sufficient |
| D9 | `ureq` + scoped threads, not `reqwest` + `tokio` | Dozens of concurrent requests, not thousands; simpler code, smaller binary, faster builds |

| D23 | Liveness is proven only by held flocks | A flock is released by the kernel on exit, so "lock free" proves the writer is gone. ## 8. Risks and open questions

- **CurseForge policy:** personal keys may be revoked or the terms enforced. Mitigated by D4 (never required).
- **Forever launch layout** (product `wowf` / `_forever_` / interface 16001 / `_Forever` suffix) is pre-launch data. Mitigated by D15 and fixtures covering both the beta and launch layouts.
- **M1 size versus the Forever date.** M1 holds the riskiest engine work. Mitigated by the M1 delivery order, which puts the Forever-critical path first.
- **Keyless coverage of the long tail** (e.g. Details! is not on GitHub releases). WoWI, URL/zip installs and optional CF cover the gap.
- **Legacy ecosystems have no registry.** Catalog entries plus git/url sources are the realistic ceiling; `ClientRules` verification guards against modern builds landing in legacy clients.
- **The main GitHub path relies on web endpoints** (302 locations, atom feeds) with undocumented secondary limits. Mitigated by `MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_HOST`, backoff, the REST/GraphQL fallbacks, and live probes at checkpoints.
- **The `product.db` field layout is UNVERIFIED.** The tolerant reader falls back to scanning.
- **`RENAME_EXCHANGE` and reflink are unavailable on some filesystems** (NTFS game drives, some FUSE). The two-rename fallback reports `atomic_swap: false`; the byte-copy fallback costs I/O for SavedVariables snapshots.
- **Wine process naming under Proton/umu is UNVERIFIED.** The `cmdline`/`environ` fallback applies; a false negative degrades to a warning, never data loss, because transactions stay atomic.
- **Mixed-version multi-folder addons.** A `/reload` during a running-client transaction can briefly load a mix; the outcome reports `reload_required`.
- **Dependency ambiguity** (781 shared WoWI folder names) is handled by ranking, single-folder preference and candidate warnings.
- **Adoption false positives** are handled by Title/Author corroboration for `UIDir`-only matches, explicit folders for `guess`, and undoable `adopt` transactions.
- **Unverified client details:** the modern `AddOns.txt` format, where the out-of-date checkbox is stored, how legacy clients handle comma Interface lists, and Turtle WoW's exe version. Features depending on them are optional or fixture-guarded.
- **Scope creep** (WeakAuras strings, profiles, TUI, MCP) is excluded by the non-goals.

## 9. Confidence assessment

- **High:**
  - reliability: transaction engine, liveness-by-flock, atomic swaps, single writer, optimistic concurrency;
  - privacy: allowlist, `net.log`, no CF caching;
  - agent ergonomics: stdout envelope on failure, argv fixes, stored plans, attribution.

  Each maps to a defect observed in the reference implementation (§3) or found in review, and each is proven by a specific test (failure injection, concurrency, hostile archives, allowlist, contract snapshots, doctor harness).
- **Medium:**
  - keyless coverage of what users actually run (strong for the most-used addons, weaker for the long tail);
  - Forever's final layout;
  - `product.db` layout and Proton process naming (both have fallbacks);
  - whether M1 lands before 2026-11-04.
- **Low:** whether CurseForge tolerates personal keys in a local tool. Nothing depends on it.

comments.text:
**D16 — No CI. A local gate runs before every commit that changes code.**

This replaces the CI references in the description: M1's scope item "CI workflow running all quality gates" and M5's "`cargo audit` in CI".

- **Repository status.** The repository stays private until the project fully works on the owner's own setup. Open-sourcing happens only once the owner is confident in the project, and CI gets reconsidered then, not before. Until that point there is no `.github/workflows/`, no hosted runner, and no CI configuration file of any kind.
- **What replaces the CI items.** M1 delivers one local command that runs the full gate. M5 runs `cargo audit` locally as part of the release checklist.
- **The rule.** Every commit that contains a code change runs the local gate first, and is committed only when the gate passes. The gate is:
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo test`
  - `ubs` on the changed files
  - `cargo deny check`, but only when `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock` changed
- **Not in the per-commit gate.** Fuzz runs, coverage, real-machine smoke tests (gated behind an environment variable) and benchmarks. These run at milestone checkpoints.
- **What counts as a code change:** any staged change to a file that is compiled into the binary or used by the build or the test suite.
  - `*.rs` files under `src/`, `tests/`, `fuzz/` and `benches/`, plus `build.rs`
  - `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `deny.toml`, and clippy/rustfmt configuration
  - Assets embedded in the binary:
    - `omarchy/**` (the QML, JS and manifest are embedded with `include_str!`)
    - `catalog/**`
    - `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (a test asserts it is identical to the `agent-guide` output)
  - Test fixtures and `insta` snapshots: `tests/fixtures/**` and `**/snapshots/**`
- **What does not count as a code change** (the gate may be skipped): `.beads/**`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore`, and any other Markdown or documentation that is not embedded in the binary.
- **Mixed commits.** A commit that contains both kinds counts as a code change.

This comment overrides parts of the description:

- In §5.8 "CLI contract", the error envelope on stdout, the `v` field, the `next` field, exit codes 0–4 and "bare `omaddons` = status" are replaced by D17–D19.
